summary: Cycle-6 focused adversarial review of KE-ENSO notebook_v2 v2.6 (tercile lens + HarvestStat 3.6-B)

verdicts.verdict: The v2.6 machinery is mechanically sound — all four hsView functions, tercByYear, makeTercileStrip, simYearSet/simMarks execute clean in node/jsdom against the real parquets for Machakos and Marsabit (0 throws, all DOM nodes; fence checker PASS; all 202 nbText refs resolve; band-scale fix verified) — but execution exposed one wrong-numbers bug (Area anomaly = area divided by the production median, e.g. "422% of a usual year"), silent dropping of real 1990 bars in five counties, a tercile-threshold callout whose mm cutoffs don't match the classification actually used, and orphaned §2 shading controls whose legend describes bands no chart draws.

verdicts.reviewer: hostile-agstats-climate-reviewer + confused-first-reader (v2.6 review, commit 1ad2045 + uncommitted band-scale fix)
verdicts.verdict: The v2.6 lag grammar itself is sound where it matters — planting-year anchoring, the OND offset −1 strip under 3.6-A (no double shift), and the 1991–2020 county terciles all verified against the parquets — but one anomaly-math bug is critical and the section restructure left a trail of dead controls and stale prose that actively misleads a first-time reader.

confirmed.title: Area (ha) anomaly is computed against the PRODUCTION median — wrong numbers displayed
confirmed.where: notebooks/KE-enso-explorer/notebook_v2.qmd:2889-2901 (hsRows), surfacing at 2944 (series tooltip), 2983/2986 (wet-dry y axis), 3019/3023 (vs-climate y), 3040 (table "% of usual year"), 1565 (CSV pct_of_usual)
confirmed.problem: hsRows maps varKey = hsVar.id === "yield_t_ha" ? "yield" : "prod", so when hsVar = Area (ha) the value d.area_ha is divided by the era median of production_t. Every "% of a usual year" figure under the Area variable — tooltips, both analytic views' y axes, the table column, and the CSV export — is a physically meaningless ratio presented as a percentage to policymakers.
confirmed.evidence: Executed hsRows verbatim in node against the real parquet: Machakos Maize Long-1991 area = 82,200 ha renders anomPct = 422%; Long-1992 61,255 ha → 315%; Long-1993 66,000 ha → 339%. The med map (2891-2892) only ever stores |yield and |prod keys; no |area median exists. DESIGN_ke18_harveststat.md §2 defines the anomaly per variable-with-a-baseline; area was never given one.
confirmed.fix: Either (a) add med.set(k + "|area", v.length >= 7 ? d3.median(v, (d) => d.area_ha) : null) and map varKey area_ha→"area", or (b) set anomPct = null when hsVar.id === "area_ha" so Area falls back to absolute-only (the contract's greyed anomaly-view behaviour) — wet-dry and vs-climate then show their honest no-baseline placeholder instead of fabricated percentages.

verify.reasoning: CONFIRMED by code read and executed reproduction. notebook_v2.qmd:2894 maps every non-yield variable to varKey "prod", but the hsVar selector (line 1521) includes {id:"area_ha"}; the med map (2891-2892) stores only |yield and |prod keys, so with Area (ha) selected, line 2901 computes d.area_ha / era-median(production_t) * 100. Reproduced against the real parquet (data/KE-enso-explorer/harveststat_county_production.parquet) with python: Machakos Maize Long era 1991–2001 has 10 qc-clean years, median production 19,457.55 t; Long-1991 area 82,200 ha → 422%, 1992 → 315%, 1993 → 339% — matching the finding exactly (honest area-vs-area figure would be 113%). All cited surfacing points verified in the file: tooltip 2944, wet-dry y 2971/2986, vs-climate y 3007/3023, table 3040, CSV 1565; the views' anomPct!=null gates do not filter out the fabricated values. DESIGN_ke18_harveststat.md (playbook/handovers/KE-enso-explorer/, line 15) confirms the contract's absolute-only/greyed fallback exists and that area was never given an anomaly baseline.
verify.fix: Prefer option (a), amended: in hsRows (notebook_v2.qmd ~2890-2894) add an area era-median and route area_ha to it — inside the eras loop add `med.set(k + "|area", v.filter((d) => d.area_ha != null).length >= 7 ? d3.median(v, (d) => d.area_ha) : null);` and change line 2894 to `const varKey = hsVar.id === "yield_t_ha" ? "yield" : hsVar.id === "area_ha" ? "area" : "prod";`. The amendment matters because the eras grouping filters rows on yield_t_ha != null, so the raw v.length>=7 gate counts yield-clean rows, not area-non-null rows; d3.median already skips nulls. This keeps all three variables symmetric with well-defined era baselines (e.g. Machakos Long 1991 becomes an honest 113% of usual). Option (b) (anomPct = null when hsVar.id === "area_ha", falling back to the contract's absolute-only behaviour) is also acceptable but strictly less informative, since area medians are computable under the same >=7-year gate.

confirmed.title: Real Short-rains 1990 harvests silently dropped by the hard-coded hsYears band domain
confirmed.where: notebooks/KE-enso-explorer/notebook_v2.qmd:2905 (hsYears = d3.range(1991, 2025)), 2930 (x domain), 2925-2926 (missing markers span hsYears only)

confirmed.evidence: duckdb: SELECT ... WHERE season IN ('Long','Short') AND planting_year < 1991 → 5 county rows, all Maize Short 1990, qc=0, four with production/yield values. Node harness OUT-OF-DOMAIN probe confirms these rows survive into hsRows for those counties while the Plot band domain excludes x=1990.
confirmed.fix: Set hsYears = d3.range(1990, 2025) (and extend the era-bracket text/hsEraOf boundary wording to 1990–2001), or derive the domain from d3.min/max of the data unioned with [1991, 2024]. Keep the hole cells as-is — 1990 is pre-hole so the missing-marker logic already handles the Long panel's empty 1990 honestly.

(1) duckdb on data/KE-enso-explorer/harveststat_county_production.parquet returns 5 Maize Short planting_year=1990 rows (Embu area-only; Kiambu 3,450 t; Kitui 21,395.7 t; Meru 15,318.9 t; Murang'a 26,184.69 t), all qc_flag=0; Short-season min py is 1990. confirmed.title: Tercile-threshold callout displays mm cutoffs from the wrong baseline — contradicts the classification every strip/bar/lens actually uses
confirmed.problem: tercThresholdLine computes lo/hi as sorted-index thirds of ALL chirps years and captions them "the bottom and top thirds of 1981–2025 — the same categories as a KMD ... outlook". But the terciles that drive simYearSet, every tercile strip, 3.5 dot fills, 3.6-A/B bar fills come from enso_outlook_base, which was baked with 1991–2020 interpolated tercile cutoffs. The reader is told drier-than-usual means "under 303 mm" in Machakos while the charts classify 279–303 mm years as Near — the notebook's own definition sentence disagrees with its own visuals. The strip legend (2853) correctly says 1991–2020, so the notebook states two different baselines for "the same categories".
confirmed.evidence: Recomputed from the parquets: Machakos OND stored terciles match 1991–2020 interpolated percentiles 45/45 (cutoffs 278.6/343.9 mm) but the callout's all-years sorted-index method gives 302.8/356.8 mm and matches only 37/45; Marsabit: 100.8/167.0 true vs 95.5/155.2 displayed (44-45/45 vs stored for 1991-2020 methods, 37/45 for the displayed one).
confirmed.fix: In tercThresholdLine, filter rows to year >= 1991 && year <= 2020 and use d3.quantile(sortedValues, 1/3) / d3.quantile(sortedValues, 2/3) (linear interpolation, matching the producer), and change the caption to "the bottom and top thirds of 1991–2020". Better: read the cutoffs from enso_outlook_base (clim fields) so notebook and producer can never drift.

(1) Code: tercThresholdLine (notebook_v2.qmd:1099-1107) sorts ALL chirpsYearlyAll years (query at 3552 has no year filter; 45 years 1981-2025) and takes sorted-index thirds rows[floor(n/3)]/rows[floor(2n/3)], captioned "bottom and top thirds of 1981–2025". (2) The classification everywhere else comes from enso_outlook_base.parquet via tercByYear (2822-2829) → simYearSet (2755-2760), strip cells (2845), 3.5 dots (1400, 2895), 3.6 bars (4348-4354). (3) Producer _sources/enso_outlook_build.py lines 27/52-59: CLIM0,CLIM1=1991,2020; np.percentile(clim,[100/3,200/3]) linear interpolation; meta.json confirms. (4) Recomputed from the parquets: Machakos OND stored terciles match the 1991-2020 percentile method 45/45 (cutoffs 278.6/343.9 mm) while the callout's method displays 302.8/356.7 mm and matches only 36/45 — e.g. 1985 (282.9 mm), 1991 (289.9), 1993 (299.9), 2025 (288.4) are charted Near but fall under the callout's 303 mm "drier" cutoff; 2024 (356.7 mm) is charted Wet but below the callout's 357 mm "wetter" cutoff. The finding's numbers were trivially off (37/45 vs 36/45, 356.8 vs 356.7, 95.5 vs 95.6) but the defect is exactly as described.
verify.fix: In tercThresholdLine (notebook_v2.qmd:1099-1107): filter to the producer's baseline and use interpolated terciles — const vals = chirpsYearlyAll.filter((d) => d.period === lensSeasonCode && d.value != null && d.year >= 1991 && d.year <= 2020).map((d) => d.value).sort((a, b) => a - b); then lo = d3.quantile(vals, 1/3), hi = d3.quantile(vals, 2/3) (d3.quantile's linear interpolation is the same R-7 method as the producer's np.percentile default — verified to reproduce the stored terciles 45/45 for Machakos and Marsabit OND). Change the caption from "1981–2025" to "the bottom and top thirds of 1991–2020" (matching tercStripLegend). AMENDMENT to the finding's "better" option: the cutoffs canNOT currently be read from enso_outlook_base — its clim_mean/clim_sd fields are the normal's mean/sd, not the tercile cutoffs; to source them from the parquet the producer (_sources/enso_outlook_build.py) would need to emit new terc_lo/terc_hi columns (t1/t2 are already computed at line 56) and the parquet rebaked. The d3.quantile recompute is the correct notebook-side fix today. Cosmetic: producer classifies Dry as v <= t1, so "under X mm" is strictly "at or under X mm".
